newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares dip, TV shares hit market.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares dip, TV shares hit market.

text.p: Egyptian share prices dipped a fraction on Monday in heavy volume dominated by the registration of newly privatised television manufacturer Telemisr/Arab Transistor Radio and Electronics Supplies.
The Capital Markets Authority (CMA) overall index closed 0.09 points down at 234.93 but brokers said the price trend was still upwards in the important cement and milling sectors.

The state sold 1.53 million shares in Telemisr, 76 percent of the company's equity, to the private sector at the fixed privatisation price of 30.00 pounds a share, pushing turnover to a high 63.41 million pounds ($18.7 million), the CMA said.
But broker Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB said the rest of the market was also very busy and the mood remained bullish.
Monopoly cigarette manufacturer Eastern Company, the most active after Telemisr, rose 1.00 to close at 45.00.
Suez Cement fell back to 46.45 from 47.01, shedding some of the gains it made after the National Bank of Egypt said it would sell the shares through a global depository receipt offering.
"I think it will settle at 46.00. It should have been at this price a while ago," said Khalil. "It's not just the GDR. It's also the performance of the company," he added.
But the other main cement companies all rose -- Egyptian Tora Portland Cement by 0.74 to 56.95, Alexandria Portland Cement to 419.00 from 415.00 and Helwan Portland Cement by 1.25 to 44.00.
In the very popular milling sector, Southern Cairo Flour Mills rose 3.20 to 50.00 on reports that the company would pay a 1995/6 dividend of around five pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell back to 352.01 from 353.81 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 160.72 from 160.73 points.
